definition: Synergistic means producing a combined effect greater than the sum of the parts' separate effects — the pieces accomplish more together than their individual results could ever add up to alone.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word synergistic. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know synergistic should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The farmer's synergistic rotation of corn and beans left the soil richer than either crop could have managed alone, and both harvests grew larger every year.
Compatible is weaker: compatible tools simply work side by side without conflict, while a synergistic pairing actually multiplies what each one can do.
Transformative is stronger: a synergistic combination boosts results beyond the sum of the parts, but a transformative one creates something entirely new that neither part resembled.

Complementary parts each supply what the other lacks, so together they make a balanced whole — a planner beside an improviser, a big-picture thinker beside a detail-checker. Synergistic makes a bolder claim: the combination does not just balance, it amplifies, producing more than the parts' separate results added together.

Reinforcing means strengthening something that already exists — each part props up the other's effect, pushing in the same direction. Synergistic claims more than added strength: the combined result outruns the simple sum of what the parts achieve apart.

Amplifying means making a result larger or stronger, and one thing can amplify another all by itself, one-directionally. Synergistic is about the pairing: the parts together generate an outcome bigger than their separate effects could ever add up to.

Formal — business, science, and policy writing
Synergistic makes a claim about the size of a combined outcome: the whole achieves more than the parts added together (1 + 1 turning out greater than 2).

Keep it distinct from symbiotic, taught in this same unit — symbiotic names the structure of an ongoing two-way relationship in which each partner benefits, while synergistic is about the amplified result of a combination.
The noun form, synergy, is common (and sometimes overused) in business writing.

The city launched its bike-share program the same spring the transit authority extended evening train service, and officials braced for the two projects to compete for riders.
The programs proved synergistic.
Riders who would never walk fifteen minutes to a station happily pedaled five, so the bikes fed the trains; late trains meant a ride home was always certain, so more people risked commuting by bike.
Transit ridership rose nineteen percent and bike trips tripled — gains that dwarfed what either project had produced in pilot tests run separately the year before.
As the transit chief put it, neither project merely helped the other along — together they multiplied each other's results.
